problem: pack masks stream lengths with & 0xFFFF instead of raising on streams over 65535 bytes, so encode of inputs of about 256 KiB or more silently corrupts data on decode.
unpack dropped the block-length and jump-table-length checks, so empty, truncated or corrupt blocks decode to wrong data without error.
pack no longer checks for exactly 4 streams, so 3 or 5 streams yield a malformed block that unpack misreads, and it is now inconsistent with join.
split no longer rejects input under MIN_SPLIT_SIZE, silently changing the documented ValueError contract for 0-3 byte inputs.
The diff removes five validation paths and adds no tests for the oversize, wrong-count, truncated-block or short-input cases.
Literals 6 and 0xFFFF replace TABLE_SIZE and MAX_TABLE_LENGTH, leaving those constants and MIN_SPLIT_SIZE unused.
The commit subject 'fourstream: rework the implementation' has no conventional type, and the repo has no CLAUDE.md to check conventions against.
